title: 5 states, blank tape. It runs 47,176,870 steps, then halts. The busy beaver.
description:
A Turing machine with five states and two symbols, run from a blank tape until it halts. Each of the ten rules says what to do when a state reads a 0 or a 1: write a symbol, move one cell left or right, switch state. The machine is 1RB1LC_1RC1RB_1RD0LE_1LA1LD_1RZ0LA, the five-state champion found by Marxen and Buntrock in 1990 and proved to be the longest-running halting five-state machine by the bbchallenge project in 2024. The simulation runs it step by step; there is no seed and no floating point, so every number is exact.

Measured:
- halts after 47,176,870 steps (the halting transition counts as a step)
- ones on the tape at the halt: 4,098
- tape cells visited: 12,289, from cell -12,243 to cell 45
- the tape first spans 100 cells at step 2,670, 1,000 cells at step 284,475, 10,000 cells at step 25,615,315
- the halting transition: state E reads a 0, writes a 1, moves right, halts
- the final tape has 8,193 runs of ones and zeros; the longest run of ones is 2, and the longest run of zeros inside the span is 2

The video plays the run on a logarithmic clock: step 1 at 1 s, step 100 at 7 s, one million at 18 s, the halt at 27 s. The space-time diagram draws one row of the whole tape per moment with time running down.

The numbers in the narration are the printed outputs of this exact run.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
